newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian profits point to growing economy.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian profits point to growing economy.

text.p: December quarter company profits data on Thursday gave further credence to the view that the Australian economy was gathering pace, analysts said.

The 8.6 percent rise in profits has led analyst to revise up gross domestic product (GDP) forecasts as the market had been expecting a result close to flat for the quarter, with the highest forecast being for a 2.5 percent rise.
While fourth quarter growth might still only be moderate, the data did fit in with the official view that growth would strengthen through 1997, analysts said.
The fact that the previous quarter's profits were revised up added to the strength in the data.

"The economy has been picking up for some time, now we're getting revisons which suggests that it's all been a little bit stronger than prehaps we anticipated, and there's not much sign of that slowing down," Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia, said.

This prospect of stronger growth through 1997 s shared by both the government and the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), and accordingly has seen expectations of another cut in interest rates wound back in recent weeks.
"The outlook now is for stronger growth during 1997 than that experienced through 1996," the RBA said in its quarterly report on the economy, released on Tuesday.
The data also supported the RBA's outlook of moderate inflation, and continuing strong business investment.
"The incentive for margin widening is not as strong as when profits are weak," Citibank Australia economists said.
"It also means that firms are cashed up, ready and able to fund this year's expected surge in investment," they said.
More immediately, the profits strength meant forecasts for fourth quarter GDP would be revised up.
Preliminary estimates suggested that the profits would add around 0.8 percent to GDP, as well as seeing previous quarters growth lifted.
"It adds a not insignificant amount to GDP," Bankers Trust Australia senior economist Peter Munckton said, although he added that fourth quarter growth would still be moderate.
"It looks like in the second half of the year we were getting moderate type growth," he said.
While it was stronger than expected, it was not inconsistent with official expectations for the year ahead.
"I don't think this changes your view on things looking forward in terms of growth profile or interest rate outlook," Munckton said.
The RBA on Tuesday said that given its outlook for stronger growth in 1997 and continued moderate inflation, current monetary policy settings were appropriate for the time being.

The RBA also said that economic growth had remained moderate, "but the data becoming available over the past couple of months have been firmer, on average, than those received during the second half of 1996."
However, some economists saw the strong profits growth and revisions as suggesting that the economy may have turned earlier than previously thought, and growth was already strengthening in late 1996.

"I think what it suggests is that the economy might have been in better shape in the second half of 1996 than many commentators, including the Reserve Bank, may have realised," Macquarie Bank senior economist John Kyriakopoulos said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
